newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Games scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish first division (current league standings in parentheses, kick-off times gmt):
Saturday:
Real Madrid (1) vs Real Betis (3) 1930 gmt
League leaders Real Madrid face one of their toughest challenges yet in a potentially decisive game against one of the best away sides in the Spanish league.
Sevilla (21) vs Tenerife (9) 2000

Sevilla players Juan Carlos Unzue and Luis Tevenet warmed up for a fixture known for its violence and sendings-off with a punch-up in training. Argentine coach Carlos Bilardo hopes to be able to sit on the Sevilla bench for the first time.
Valencia (11) vs Zaragoza (18) 2015

Strikers Claudio Lopez and Gabriel Moya are doubtful for Valencia, where president Paco Roig is under heavy fire from fans, while Zaragoza are showing signs of reviving under Luis Costa, their third manager of the season.
Sunday
Logrones (19) vs Compostela (17) 1600
Compostela, who have lost all their first division visits to Logrones, will need to shake off a dressing room upheaval which has left four players being fined.
Sporting Gijon (15) vs Real Sociedad (4) 1600

Sporting are hoping for one of their three goalkeepers to recover from injury in a game for which the club has lowered ticket prices in a bid to attract fans. Real Sociedad may drop midfielder Javi de Pedro, in favour of Mutiu Adepojo.
Barcelona (2) vs Racing Santander (8) 1600

Ronaldo's trip to the Rio carnival is thought to have caused unease in the Barcelona camp, where beleaguered coach Bobby Robson will fight for his managerial life against a side that squeezed a draw out of their last visit to the Nou Camp.
Valladolid (7) vs Espanyol (13) 1600
Valladolid have overcome an injury crisis and have Jose Quevedo and Raul Ibanez back from suspension for a game against an Espanyol side boosted by last week's victory over Barcelona.
Athletic Bilbao (10) vs Oviedo (12) 1600
The Athletic coaching staff have come out in defence of heavily-criticised goalkeeper Juan Valenica ahead of a game which both sides must win to keep distant UEFA Cup hopes alive.
Extremadura (22) vs Rayo Vallecano (16) 1600

Rayo needed a last-minute penalty to take the recent Cup tie with Extremadura, whose fans will show their displeasure with a series of controversial refereeing decisions by waving black handkerchiefs.
Celta Vigo (14) vs Hercules (20) 1600
Hercules coach Quique Hernandez may lose troubled Peruvian striker Flavio Maestri through injury, while top Celta striker Juan Sanchez is also a doubtful starter.
Deportivo Coruna (5) vs Atletico Madrid (6) 1830

Radomir Antic will not be on the Atletico bench for a game that Deportivo must play away in Santiago -- fulfilling in both cases punishments decreed months ago. New Deportivo coach Carlos Alberto Silva has decided to watch the game from the stands.
